paragraphs: Adaptive tests aim to estimate a student's ability using a carefully chosen sequence of questions. The difficulty is deciding whether a short test produces an accurate estimate when true ability is not directly observable. This paper addresses that problem by analyzing the estimate that would be obtained from responses to the entire question bank as a theoretical approximation of true ability.

The proposed BECAT framework selects a smaller collection of questions whose estimation gradient closely matches that of the full responses. In plain terms, the selected questions should push the ability estimate in much the same direction as the complete bank would. An approximation to the expected gradient difference makes this idea usable through a simple greedy selection algorithm.

The authors provide theoretical guarantees, including an upper bound on estimation error. Experiments on real and synthetic datasets reach the same estimation accuracy with 15% fewer questions on average. This links shorter tests to an explicit accuracy objective, while retaining the distinction between true ability and its full-response approximation.
neurips-2023-a-bounded-ability-estimatio.tldr: BECAT selects questions to approximate full-bank ability estimation, achieving the same accuracy with 15% fewer questions on average in experiments.

paragraphs: Training an AI to cooperate with unfamiliar humans without human training data requires exposing it to different partner behaviors. Existing population-based approaches do this by first building a collection of distinct policies. E3T addresses the computational expense of that preparation by training the cooperating agent directly with a partner policy constructed during the learning process.

That partner combines the agent's own policy with a random policy. The mixture supplies both coordination ability and behavioral variety without requiring a separately pretrained population. E3T also includes a partner-modeling component that predicts the partner's next action using historical information. The agent can use this prediction to adjust its actions when facing different patterns of human behavior.

Experiments in Overcooked show substantially improved training efficiency while maintaining performance comparable to or better than the population-based baselines. The result supports the use of a simple mixture as a practical source of partner diversity in this setting. Partner prediction adds a complementary mechanism for responding to the particular collaborator encountered during execution.
neurips-2023-an-efficient-end-to-end-tra.tldr: E3T trains agents with mixed self-and-random partners, improving training efficiency for human–AI coordination in Overcooked.

paragraphs: Finding an equilibrium does not by itself identify the equilibrium that best serves a chosen objective. This paper develops a learning-based approach to that optimization problem in games with sequential decisions. Its scope includes any number of players and several equilibrium concepts, alongside applications to mechanism design and information design.

The central observation is that optimal equilibria can be represented as minimax equilibrium strategies of a player in an extensive-form zero-sum game. This reformulation makes methods for learning in zero-sum games available for the original problem. The authors obtain learning dynamics that converge to optimal equilibria both in empirical averages and in the individual iterates produced during learning.

That distinction matters because convergence of averages alone does not establish convergence of the successive strategies themselves. The paper also demonstrates practical flexibility through state-of-the-art performance on benchmark tabular games and an optimal sequential-auction mechanism computed with deep reinforcement learning. Together, these results connect a broadly applicable mathematical reformulation with concrete equilibrium and mechanism computations.
neurips-2023-computing-optimal-equilibri.tldr: Recasting optimal-equilibrium computation as zero-sum learning yields convergence of both averaged strategies and individual iterates.

paragraphs: An agent serving several objectives must decide how to combine them across time. This becomes difficult when the objectives use different discount factors, meaning they place different weight on future outcomes. The paper studies what consistent aggregation should require, starting from a set of normative axioms rather than choosing a combination rule solely for convenience.

Under those axioms, the authors show that Markovian reward functions cannot be aggregated into a Markovian reward when objectives may have different time preferences. Here, the relevant distinction is whether aggregation can rely on the current information used by the individual objectives or must also admit dependence beyond it. The necessity of non-Markovian rewards follows within this axiomatic setting.

The paper then proposes a practical aggregation scheme that accommodates this dependence using one additional parameter per objective. Its contribution is both a constraint on how consistent aggregation can work and a constructive way to address that constraint. This is relevant to agents serving stakeholders, including successive generations, whose preferences about timing differ.
neurips-2023-consistent-aggregation-of-o.tldr: Under the paper's axioms, combining objectives with different discount factors requires non-Markovian rewards.

paragraphs: Adversarial images are designed to mislead a neural network, but optimizing only for that goal can produce changes that depart from natural imagery. The resulting tension is between attack effectiveness and visual stealthiness. This paper introduces Diffusion-Based Projected Gradient Descent, or Diff-PGD, to generate effective adversarial samples that remain close to the original data distribution.

Diff-PGD uses guidance from a diffusion model in the gradient-based generation process. The framework also separates optimization of the adversarial objective from auxiliary objectives such as content preservation, smoothness, or style. The authors describe this separation as making generation more stable and controllable, and show how the framework can be customized for digital, physical-world, and style-based attacks.

The reported findings include better transferability and greater resistance to purification than traditional gradient-based methods. These results concern whether generated attacks remain effective beyond their immediate construction setting and after purification is applied. The contribution combines natural-looking generation with control over additional image properties, rather than treating every desired property as part of one coupled optimization.
neurips-2023-diffusion-based-adversarial.tldr: Diff-PGD uses diffusion guidance to generate effective, natural-looking adversarial images with improved controllability and reported transferability.

paragraphs: Q-learning depends on estimates of how valuable actions will be. This paper shows that using deep neural networks introduces two sources of Gumbel-distributed noise into that process. The noise is heteroscedastic, meaning its variability is not constant. Double Gumbel Q-Learning, also called DoubleGum, explicitly accounts for these two sources when constructing its learning objective.

The treatment differs between discrete and continuous action spaces. For discrete control, the authors derive a closed-form loss. For continuous control, the corresponding loss is intractable, so they derive an approximation. That approximation includes a hyperparameter controlling pessimism, allowing the learning procedure to regulate how conservatively it treats action-value estimates.

Using a proposed default setting, DoubleGum outperforms the listed comparison methods in aggregate across 33 tasks from four control suites. Aggregate superiority does not imply a win on every task. The authors also show that tuning the pessimism parameter may improve sample efficiency further. The findings connect an explicit noise model to a practical control algorithm with a usable default configuration.
neurips-2023-double-gumbel-q-learning-4e.tldr: DoubleGum models two Gumbel noise sources in deep Q-learning and reports stronger aggregate performance across 33 control tasks.

paragraphs: A useful uncertainty estimate should express how a model's uncertainty relates across multiple inputs. This paper evaluates that capability through joint predictions of labels, rather than considering each prediction in isolation. Large ensembles can provide such predictions, but running and training many constituent models can make the computational cost prohibitive.

The authors introduce the epinet, an architecture that can be added to a conventional neural network, including a large pretrained model. It is trained with modest additional computation to estimate uncertainty. In the reported comparisons, networks equipped with an epinet outperform very large ensembles containing hundreds or more particles while using orders of magnitude less computation.

The paper also introduces epistemic neural networks, or ENNs, as a general interface for models producing joint predictions. This broader interface accommodates the epinet, which does not fit the traditional Bayesian neural-network framework. The contribution therefore combines a concrete architecture for computationally efficient uncertainty estimation with a way to describe and develop a wider family of joint-prediction models.
neurips-2023-epistemic-neural-networks-7.tldr: An epinet adds efficient joint uncertainty predictions to conventional networks, outperforming much larger ensembles in the reported comparisons.

paragraphs: Lossy compression trades a smaller representation against some distortion of the original data. The rate-distortion function describes the fundamental relationship between these quantities for a data source. Estimating it provides a reference for what compression algorithms could achieve, rather than measuring only the performance of one particular compressor.

This paper estimates that function using optimal transport and Wasserstein gradient descent. The classic Blahut–Arimoto approach fixes the possible values of the reproduction distribution in advance. The proposed method instead moves particles to learn where those values should lie. The authors prove local convergence and analyze sample complexity through a connection to entropic optimal transport.

On low-rate sources, the experiments produce bounds comparable to or tighter than those from state-of-the-art neural approaches, with substantially less tuning and computation. The convergence claim is local, while the empirical comparison concerns the tested low-rate setting. The paper additionally connects the estimator to maximum-likelihood deconvolution and introduces sources with known rate-distortion solutions, providing further test cases for evaluating estimators.
neurips-2023-estimating-the-rate-distort.tldr: Moving particles with Wasserstein gradient descent estimates compression limits while learning the reproduction distribution's support.

paragraphs: Exact Bayesian inference computes posterior quantities without the approximation error associated with sampling-based estimates. This paper develops an exact method for a large class of discrete statistical models, including supported problems with infinitely many possible outcomes and continuous priors. A probabilistic programming language expresses models using sampling, discrete observations, affine functions, branching, and conditioning on discrete events.

The central representation is a probability generating function, which compactly encodes distributions described by these programs. This representation enables exact calculation of posterior probabilities, means, variances, and higher moments. The authors prove the method correct and automate it in Genfer, a tool using automatic differentiation with Taylor polynomials rather than requiring computer algebra.

Experiments show that Genfer is often faster than the existing exact tools PSI, Dice, and Prodigy. On a range of real-world problems those tools cannot solve, its performance is competitive with approximate Monte Carlo methods while avoiding their approximation errors. The findings demonstrate that exact inference can be computationally practical for the model class handled by this representation.
neurips-2023-exact-bayesian-inference-on.tldr: Genfer uses probability generating functions to automate exact Bayesian inference for a broad class of discrete models.

paragraphs: Many forecasting applications begin with very short observation histories, sometimes 40 points or fewer. Methods that depend on substantial task-specific training data are difficult to apply in that setting. ForecastPFN addresses this problem through zero-shot forecasting: a pretrained model predicts a new series without first undergoing a separate training procedure for that dataset.

The model is trained entirely on a newly designed synthetic data distribution. As a prior-data fitted network, it learns to approximate Bayesian inference and can produce predictions for a new time-series dataset in one forward pass. This shifts the training burden into advance preparation on synthetic series, allowing the deployed predictor to work directly with the observations available.

The authors report experiments in which ForecastPFN is both more accurate and faster than state-of-the-art forecasting methods. The comparisons include cases where competing methods can train on hundreds of additional points from the target distribution. These empirical findings support synthetic pretraining as an effective route to forecasting with scarce initial data in the evaluated settings.
neurips-2023-forecastpfn-synthetically-t.tldr: ForecastPFN learns from synthetic series to deliver fast zero-shot forecasts, outperforming the compared methods in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: An AI agent may have an incentive to deceive if doing so helps it achieve its objective. The paper highlights an especially revealing example: language models pursuing the goal of being judged truthful can still exhibit deception. Studying that behavior requires a definition that applies to learning agents and captures more than whether an isolated statement is false.

The authors formulate deception within structural causal games, grounding their definition in philosophical work. This supplies a common mathematical setting for reasoning about agents, their objectives, and causal relationships. Examples and formal results are used to show that the definition agrees with philosophical and everyday understandings of deception.

The main technical contribution is a set of graphical criteria for deception. These criteria make the causal structure useful for identifying circumstances relevant to deceptive behavior. Experiments show that the resulting insights can mitigate deception in both reinforcement learning agents and language models. The contribution connects a formal account of the behavior with demonstrated mitigation, without claiming that deception is universally eliminated.
neurips-2023-honesty-is-the-best-policy-.tldr: The paper defines deception in causal games and derives graphical criteria used experimentally to reduce deceptive AI behavior.

paragraphs: Camera-based bird's-eye-view perception must detect objects accurately while meeting tight latency requirements. Reducing a model's arithmetic workload does not by itself establish how quickly it will run on a vehicle's hardware. HotBEV therefore makes actual device latency a central design objective, considering memory access costs and the amount of work GPUs can perform in parallel.

The authors develop a theoretical latency prediction model and efficient building operators informed by these hardware properties. They use those operators in a backbone that proceeds from local to global visual modeling while capturing and combining features. These components form a hardware-oriented framework for camera-based bird's-eye-view detection.

On a V100 GPU, the paper reports NDS gains of 2%–23%, mAP gains of 2%–7.8%, and speedups of 1.1–3.4 times over existing approaches. Across additional GPU devices, reported speedups range from 1.1–6.3 times. These measurements support the premise that hardware-aware architecture design can improve detection quality and realized speed together, with the gains varying across comparisons and devices.
neurips-2023-hotbev-hardware-oriented-tr.tldr: HotBEV designs camera-based 3D detection around GPU latency, reporting improvements in both detection accuracy and measured speed.

paragraphs: Solar irradiance varies in ways that complicate the integration of solar power into electricity grids. A forecast based only on a station's time series may miss useful information about clouds and surrounding conditions. This paper develops a deep learning architecture that incorporates spatial and temporal context from satellite data for day-ahead forecasting, emphasizing Global Horizontal Irradiance.

The approach also extracts a predictive distribution for each forecast time step, providing uncertainty information alongside the forecast. Its evaluation separates difficult examples from easier ones, with changing cloud conditions defining particularly important challenging days. This makes performance in demanding conditions visible instead of folding it entirely into an overall result.

The authors additionally introduce a multimodal dataset combining satellite imagery over a large area with irradiance and related physical measurements from geographically diverse stations. They report robust forecasting performance, including zero-shot tests at stations not observed during training. The findings support using surrounding visual context for forecasts that transfer across locations, while the uncertainty estimates and difficulty-aware evaluation address how those forecasts can be assessed.
neurips-2023-improving-day-ahead-solar-i.tldr: Satellite context improves day-ahead solar forecasting, with uncertainty estimates and reported generalization to unseen stations.

paragraphs: Neural radiance fields can generate new views of a scene, but changing camera distance can expose jagged or blurry rendering artifacts. Mip-NeRF addresses this aliasing problem using integrated positional encodings, while relying on an architecture that does not obtain the fast training of grid-based methods. Mip-Grid brings anti-aliasing into grid representations to combine these advantages.

The method starts with a shared grid and creates multiple grids through simple convolutions. A scale-aware coordinate then retrieves features appropriate to the rendering scale. Despite using these multiple derived grids, the underlying representation remains a single shared grid, and the method uses a single-sampling approach. The authors report only small additions to parameters and computation.

The technique is incorporated into TensoRF and K-Planes, two representative grid-based methods. Experiments show substantial rendering improvements for both, with performance comparable to mip-NeRF on multiscale datasets and significantly faster training. These results indicate that scale-aware filtering can address aliasing while preserving the practical training advantage that motivates grid-based scene representations.
neurips-2023-mip-grid-anti-aliased-grid-.tldr: Mip-Grid adds scale-aware anti-aliasing to fast grid-based radiance fields with little additional model or computational cost.

paragraphs: Cooperative agents trained with one team composition can struggle when their teammates change. Even training on several fixed compositions may leave policies overly dependent on those particular teams. This paper augments the reward with a mutual-information term designed to discourage excessive reliance on team-related information and encourage behavior that works across different compositions.

Optimizing that objective off-policy is difficult because it involves a marginal distribution that changes during learning. The authors first analyze a version with a fixed marginal distribution, proving convergence and optimality for its policy-iteration algorithm. For practical training, they then use the Blahut–Arimoto algorithm and an imaginary distribution over team compositions to work with an approximate marginal.

Experiments show strong zero-shot generalization to changing team compositions in complex cooperative tasks. The theoretical result belongs to the fixed-marginal formulation, while the practical implementation uses approximation to address the harder optimization problem. Together, the results provide a principled objective for reducing dependence on familiar teams and empirical evidence that its implementation can improve adaptability.
neurips-2023-mutual-information-regulari.tldr: Mutual-information regularization encourages cooperative policies that generalize to changing teams, with guarantees for a fixed-marginal formulation.

paragraphs: Multi-task representation learning uses several source tasks to learn shared features, then trains a predictor on those features for a target task. This paper asks how accurately the target predictor can learn as its number of training examples grows. The analysis makes the benefit of learning a shared representation explicit through statistical bounds on excess risk.

Under regularity assumptions on the loss and assumptions about task diversity, the authors derive rates that adapt to the difficulty of the learning problem. With m target examples, these rates interpolate between the usual order of one over the square root of m and the faster order of one over m. Calling the rates optimistic means easier problems can receive stronger guarantees.

The paper also derives optimistic excess-risk rates for the source tasks themselves. Supporting contributions include a local Rademacher complexity theorem and a chain rule for composite predictor classes. These tools help analyze the shared representation and the predictor built on top of it, extending the contribution beyond the target-task bound alone.
neurips-2023-optimistic-rates-for-multi-.tldr: Under loss-regularity and task-diversity assumptions, shared representations yield target-task learning rates that improve with problem difficulty.

paragraphs: CLIP representations combine different image properties in ways that can make particular attributes difficult to isolate. An image's objects, actions, and appearance may receive uneven or unpredictable emphasis. This paper uses associations between grammatical categories and visual properties, such as nouns with objects and adjectives with appearance, to separate these sources of variation.

The authors formulate a component-analysis model that learns subspaces emphasizing variation linked to a chosen part of speech while reducing variation linked to the others. The resulting representations can be obtained in closed form and respect the geometry of the underlying representation manifold. The same framework can also learn subspaces associated with particular visual appearances, including artists' painting styles.

Experiments assess the subspaces through visualizations, class-invariance measures, and improvements to baseline zero-shot classification. The paper also demonstrates selective removal of visual themes from CLIP-based image synthesis, including preventing imitation of artists' styles in the evaluations. These findings connect more separated representations with practical control over both recognition and generated visual appearance.
neurips-2023-parts-of-speechgrounded-sub.tldr: Parts-of-speech-guided subspaces separate CLIP attributes and enable selective control over visual themes in image synthesis.

paragraphs: Computer vision pipelines commonly resize every image to a fixed resolution before processing it. NaViT revisits this choice by using the sequence-based structure of Vision Transformers, which can accommodate different sequence lengths. Its training procedure packs sequences so that images with different resolutions and aspect ratios can be processed without imposing one fixed image shape.

The authors demonstrate improved training efficiency for both large-scale supervised learning and contrastive image–text pretraining. They also show that the resulting model can be transferred efficiently to image classification, video classification, object detection, and semantic segmentation. Reported improvements on robustness and fairness benchmarks extend the evaluation beyond the primary training objectives.

Resolution flexibility also remains useful at inference time. Adjusting input resolution provides a smooth way to trade computational cost against performance, rather than committing to one operating point. The contribution connects a different treatment of image inputs with training efficiency, broad task transfer, and deployment flexibility. The authors present it as a promising direction for Vision Transformers.
neurips-2023-patch-n-pack-navit-a-vision.tldr: NaViT packs variable-sized image sequences to improve training efficiency and enable flexible inference cost–performance trade-offs.

paragraphs: Aligning a language-model assistant often requires extensive human annotations or feedback. SELF-ALIGN reduces that dependence by combining a small amount of human-written guidance with responses generated by the model itself. The goal is to teach helpful, ethical, and reliable behavior while reducing the cost and quality challenges associated with large supervision collections.

The process first generates synthetic prompts and broadens their topics. Human-written principles and demonstrations then guide the model to produce aligned responses. Those responses become fine-tuning data, allowing the resulting model to answer directly without receiving the principles and demonstrations each time. A final refinement step addresses answers that are too brief or indirect.

Applied to LLaMA-65b, the approach produces the Dromedary assistant using fewer than 300 lines of human annotations, including seed prompts, 16 principles, and five examples. Dromedary significantly exceeds several compared systems, including Text-Davinci-003 and Alpaca, on the reported benchmarks. The findings support principle-guided synthetic supervision as an effective alignment approach in these evaluations, while still relying on a small human-authored foundation.
neurips-2023-principle-driven-self-align.tldr: SELF-ALIGN turns a small set of human principles and examples into synthetic training data for the Dromedary assistant.

paragraphs: Detecting unfamiliar object categories in 3D point clouds is difficult when only a few labeled examples are available. This paper focuses on improving the latent features used by the detector. Its prototypical variational autoencoder, P-VAE, learns a probabilistic feature space intended to make sampled features both diverse and distinguishable.

The model uses a posterior resembling a mixture of Gaussian distributions, with each component centered on a prototype. A reconstruction task helps preserve geometric information. The detector applies this idea at two levels: a geometry-focused version assists feature extraction from the scene, then a category-focused version refines object-instance features after the geometry-informed features have been clustered.

This sequence gives geometric structure and object-category information distinct roles in the detection process. On two few-shot 3D detection benchmarks, the authors report performance above the compared state-of-the-art approaches. Ablation experiments and qualitative prototype analysis further support the contribution of probabilistic modeling to prototype learning. The results connect richer prototype-based features with improved detection when annotations for new categories are scarce.
neurips-2023-prototypical-variational-au.tldr: Probabilistic prototypes enrich geometry and category features, improving few-shot 3D object detection on two benchmarks.

paragraphs: Reconstructing a scene or rendering new views from limited images benefits from learned geometric structure. This paper develops a way to learn that structure using only relative camera poses while remaining consistent under changes of coordinate frame. Its key setting is the space of rays in 3D, rather than a fixed canonical frame for the scene.

The authors model ray space mathematically under SE(3), the transformations consisting of 3D rotations and translations. They construct equivariant convolutions that map ray-based information either to other rays or to 3D locations. Equivariance means the outputs transform consistently when the coordinate frame changes. The framework also supports equivariant attention, enabling a transformer in ray space.

The paper adapts these operations to multiview 3D reconstruction and neural rendering. Experiments on rotated and translated datasets show robust results without transformation augmentation. These findings demonstrate the value of incorporating coordinate-frame consistency directly into the model's operations, with relative camera poses supplying the geometric relationships needed by the proposed approach.
neurips-2023-se-3-equivariant-convolutio.tldr: Ray-space convolutions and attention build rotation-and-translation equivariance into multiview reconstruction and neural rendering.

paragraphs: Backtracking line search automatically chooses a step size for optimization and can match the performance of a theoretically optimal choice. Giving each coordinate its own step size offers a more flexible update, but makes the search harder. This paper develops multidimensional backtracking for smooth convex problems, with guarantees relative to the best diagonal preconditioner.

A diagonal preconditioner is the collection of these individual coordinate step sizes. The authors' key observation is that gradients with respect to the step sizes, called hyper-gradients, provide separating hyperplanes. These boundaries allow cutting-plane methods to narrow the search for good choices. Because generic cutting-plane algorithms would be too expensive, the paper develops an efficient algorithm tailored to this problem.

The resulting method requires no manual tuning and is provably competitive with the best diagonal preconditioner. That guarantee extends the automatic-selection principle of ordinary backtracking to a multidimensional choice. Its stated scope is smooth convex optimization, where the analysis supports comparing automatically selected coordinate scales with the strongest diagonal choice.
neurips-2023-searching-for-optimal-per-c.tldr: Multidimensional backtracking automatically selects coordinate-wise step sizes with guarantees against the best diagonal preconditioner for smooth convex problems.

paragraphs: Distributional reinforcement learning has shown empirical success, but understanding when it offers an advantage requires more specific guarantees. This paper provides small-loss bounds: guarantees that depend on the optimal achievable cost of the problem. When that cost is small, the derived bounds converge much faster than those from non-distributional approaches.

The analysis begins with a distributional contextual-bandit algorithm, DistCB. It receives small-loss regret guarantees and outperforms the compared state-of-the-art approach on three real-world tasks. For online reinforcement learning, the authors build confidence sets through maximum likelihood estimation and prove small-loss learning guarantees in low-rank Markov decision processes. They also introduce a distributional complexity measure to support the analysis.

For offline reinforcement learning, a pessimistic distributional method obtains small-loss guarantees that are more robust to poor single-policy coverage. The contribution therefore spans bandits and both online and offline learning, with different constructions for each setting. Its central explanation is conditional: distributional methods can obtain especially favorable guarantees when the best achievable cost is already low.
neurips-2023-the-benefits-of-being-distr.tldr: Small-loss bounds explain a distributional reinforcement-learning advantage when the optimal achievable cost is low.

paragraphs: Sequential recommenders learn from relationships between items in a user's interaction history. That training signal can be unreliable when a user clicks something inconsistent with their actual preferences. The resulting mismatch can affect either the contextual items supplied as input or the target the model is asked to predict, so correcting only one side leaves part of the problem untreated.

This paper theoretically analyzes how recommender predictions relate to the reliability of training instances. From that relationship, the authors derive separate error-bounded strategies for correcting unreliable inputs and targets. They combine the strategies in BirDRec, a model-agnostic framework that can be incorporated into most existing sequential recommendation systems.

A rectification sampling strategy and a self-ensemble mechanism reduce the framework's time and space costs. Experiments on four real-world datasets support its generality, effectiveness, and efficiency. The contribution provides theoretical support for using predictions to assess unreliable data, then applies that support to corrections on both sides of the training pair rather than assuming every observed interaction is trustworthy.
neurips-2023-theoretically-guaranteed-bi.tldr: BirDRec uses error-bounded corrections for both unreliable inputs and targets in sequential recommendation.

paragraphs: Automatically generated code can carry social biases, making evaluation of these systems about more than whether a program works. This paper examines that problem in pretrained code-generation models. The authors introduce a way to construct code prompts that exposes biased behavior, turning a broad concern about generated software into something that can be systematically investigated.

To measure the issue, they develop a dataset and three metrics. These measures address both overall social bias and more detailed unfairness across demographic groups. Looking at both levels matters because a single overall assessment cannot describe all of the differences between groups that the evaluation is designed to capture.

Experiments cover Codex, InCoder, and CodeGen at varying model sizes and reveal severe social biases in the tested models. Further analysis provides insights intended to help choose models with lower social bias. The paper's contribution is an evaluation approach and evidence of the problem in these systems, supplying a basis for comparing generated code along a social dimension as well as its technical usefulness.
neurips-2023-uncovering-and-quantifying-.tldr: A new prompt-construction approach, dataset, and three metrics expose severe social biases in three tested code-generation model families.
